units.summary: Every catalog: specifier, in the manifests and in pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides, names an entry in pnpm-workspace.yaml's default catalog
units.evidence: pnpm-workspace.yaml:18-64 (catalog), :78-82 (overrides using catalog:); 123 "catalog:" specs across the manifests; pnpm install fails on a missing catalog entry
units.alint: constraint reference: (dependency name whose value is catalog:) -> keys of pnpm-workspace.yaml $.catalog
units.reason: R7 lookup, as in the batch-1 twin trpc-10. The target side is YAML map keys, which JSONPath cannot select. A text regex cannot isolate the catalog block's keys from the overrides and allowBuilds keys at the same indent, so it is not expressible today.

changes.why: Stage A says no regex can isolate the catalog keys. That is refuted at this pin by a value-shape capture trick. A cross_file superset with source pnpm-workspace.yaml and regex "(?m)^  '?([@a-z0-9][^':\\s]*)'?: [~^]?[0-9][^\\s]*$" captures only catalog keys, because catalog values are unquoted version specs while overrides are quoted and allowBuilds/lockfile values are booleans. Targets are the manifests (regex '"([^"]+)"\s*:\s*"catalog:"'); a second rule takes the pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides (regex "(?m)^  '?([^'\\s:]+)'?: '?catalog:'?\\s*$"). Both rules pass on the clone. On scratch they fired on a deleted solid-js entry (3 errors), on 'nx': 'catalog:' (an allowBuilds key, 1 error) and on chokidar: 'catalog:' in overrides (1 error). They give a false positive when a catalog value is quoted, so the rule is layout-dependent and awkward: C, as for zulip-39's capture trick. This differs from trpc-10, whose file layout may not allow the trick.

tanstack-query-va-root-no-prod-dependencies (dep-version): sherif root-package-dependencies, a warning that does not fail test:sherif

tanstack-query-va-gha-all-actions-sha-pinned (other): every action, actions/* included, is SHA-pinned. This is renovate's helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests state and is stricter than zizmor's default
tanstack-query-va-eslint-rules-documented (other): every eslint-plugin-query rule has a docs/eslint/<rule>.md page
absent_categories: locale: no locale catalogs, translation files or i18n tooling (docs and UI strings are English-only), so the locale family is empty
hooks: no husky, lefthook, pre-commit, lint-staged or simple-git-hooks
other CI systems: GitHub Actions only (.nx/workflows/dynamic-changesets.yaml only sizes Nx Cloud agents); no GitLab, CircleCI, Azure, Jenkins or Buildkite
Makefile / justfile / Taskfile: none; tasks are package.json scripts plus nx targets
toolchain pin files: no .node-version, .tool-versions, Volta, engines.node or setup-node literal; Node is pinned only in .nvmrc, and pnpm via packageManager + engines.pnpm
dedicated dep-version tools besides sherif: no syncpack, manypkg or yarn constraints; pnpm catalogMode strict is not set, so catalog use is not mandated
codegen freshness gate: the TypeDoc reference pages are regenerated and auto-committed on push by autofix.ci, never diffed in a PR
per-file license headers / SPDX: none (root MIT LICENSE; packages declare "license": "MIT")
import / layering firewall: only oxlint no-restricted-syntax rules (D)
dependency license-compliance or audit gate: none
editorconfig enforcement: .editorconfig is ungated (editorconfig_conforms gives 589 findings at the pin); oxfmt is the real formatting gate
CODEOWNERS exists but gates nothing on its own
file-graph: no cycle or orphan gate; the edge sources are verify-links.ts (markdown links, docs -> docs and docs -> examples dirs) and the docs/config.json route registry, both B-adapter
unusual: CONTRIBUTING.md asks automated agents to add three robot emoji to PR or issue titles so their work is 'fast-tracked'. It is a canary that labels agent-authored contributions, not a validation

pr.yml runs every check through `nx affected` on Nx Cloud agents. The root-project targets (sherif, knip, docs links) run only when a root-owned file changes, such as pnpm-lock.yaml or docs/. test:ci (nx run-many) is defined, but no workflow calls it
CONTRIBUTING says 'We use pnpm v11', but packageManager pins pnpm@12.18.0 and engines.pnpm is >=12.18.0 (unenforced doc drift)

A TypeScript compatibility matrix through npm aliases (typescript57, 58, 59, 70 and a 7.1 dev build) in root devDependencies drives per-package test:types:tsXX scripts; sherif's `-i typescript` exempts typescript from the version-consistency rule

knip.ts imports five package.json files and derives ignoreDependencies from their optionalDependencies / peerDependenciesMeta, so that removing a declaration still fails knip --strict. Deleting those fields outright would crash the config load
The changesets fixed group 1 includes the private @tanstack/angular-query-persist-client, which sits at 5.103.2 while the rest of the group is at 5.107.1

examples/vue/2.6-basic and 2.7-basic are excluded from the pnpm workspace and pinned to @tanstack/vue-query ^5.105.0 (stale). Every in-workspace example tracks ^<current version>; 447 of 447 internal-dependency specs follow this
scripts/verify-links.ts implements site-route semantics: it appends .md to extensionless links and rewrites docs/framework/<fw>/examples/<x> to the examples/<fw>/<x> directory
scripts/generate-labeler-config.ts writes labeler-config.yml, but nothing runs it and there is no labeler workflow (an orphan script)

pnpm supply-chain hardening in pnpm-workspace.yaml: minimumReleaseAge 1440, trustPolicy no-downgrade with three named semver/ua-parser exemptions, blockExoticSubdeps, an allowBuilds allowlist and cleanupUnusedCatalogs

The install and Node setup logic lives in external SHA-pinned composite actions (TanStack/config/.github/setup and changeset-preview), so the repo's own CI files do not show how Node and pnpm are provisioned

oxlint loads ESLint plugins (eslint-plugin-jsdoc, @cspell/eslint-plugin, testing-library, a local plugin wrapping ESLint's no-restricted-syntax) as JS plugins, including a grandfathering policy for deprecated QueryClient methods
AGENTS.md and AI_POLICY.md govern AI-assisted contributions; .coderabbit.yaml enables 'slop_detection' AI review against CONTRIBUTING.md (advisory: request_changes_workflow false)

changes.detail: Stage B found a false positive: a body line such as '"Note": this is prose' fired the rule. I reproduced it with the Stage A config. The target regex now extracts only `name: major|minor|patch|none` lines, and it also accepts plain keys that are not quoted. The root package.json ('root') was dropped from the source union, because changesets does not count the root as a workspace package (this is from tool knowledge, not checked). Scratch results: the body-note line, a double-quoted valid key and an empty changeset give 0 findings. '@tanstack/query-cor', 'root' and a plain unknown key 'nonexistent-pkg' each give 1 error. The rule passes on the clone.

Replaces the for_each_match rule tanstack-query-changesets-valid-bump. Stage B found that rule fired on body prose (I reproduced it) and that it accepted a file with no frontmatter. The new rule is a file_content_matches over .changeset/*.md, excluding README.md. It requires the file to start with a ---...--- block, and every line in that block must be a blank line or a `'name'|"name"|plain-name: major|minor|patch|none` entry. Scratch results: the bump word 'bugfix', a file with no frontmatter and an unquoted '@tanstack/query-core: patch' (not valid YAML) each give 1 error. The body-note line, an empty '---\n---' changeset, a double-quoted key and a README.md give 0. A comment at the rule says it is unverified whether changesets itself rejects an unknown bump word, so the enum may be stricter than the tool. The rule passes on the clone.

The root package.json was dropped from the source union, for the same reason as tq-31. Scratch results: 'root' in config.json ignore gives 1 error, and the misspelling '@tanstack/vue-qery-devtools' in the fixed group gives 1 error. The rule passes on the clone.

Stage B found an alias false positive. I reproduced it: the Stage A rule fired on a valid 'core-alias': 'workspace:@tanstack/query-core@*'. The target regex now extracts the key only for range-form specs, matching '"workspace:[*^~<>=0-9][^"@]*"'. Aliased specs (workspace:name@range) and relative-path specs (workspace:../x) are no longer read as names. The comment now states the verified counts: 101 specs (90 workspace:*, 11 workspace:^), 66 in packages/* and 35 in integrations/*/*. Scratch results: an unknown name gives 1 error, a dependency on the excluded examples/vue/2.6-basic gives 1 error, and the excluded 2.7-basic also correctly gives 1. A valid alias, a real example name and a workspace:../ path spec each give 0. The rule passes on the clone.

Covers the aliased leg that the narrowed rule above leaves out: the aliased name in 'workspace:<name>@<range>' must be a workspace project. There are none at the pin. Scratch results: 'workspace:@tanstack/query-cor@*' and 'workspace:nope@^' each give 1 error, and a valid alias gives 0. The rule passes on the clone.

Stage B reclassified tq-15 to C and showed that a value-shape regex trick expresses it. This is a cross_file superset. The source is the indent-2 pnpm-workspace.yaml keys whose values are unquoted version specs, which captures only the catalog. The targets are the '"name": "catalog:"' (or catalog:default) entries of the workspace manifests, 123 at the pin. Level is error, with a comment explaining why it is C. Scratch results: deleting solid-js from the catalog gives 3 errors, '"nx": "catalog:"' gives 1 error and 'left-pad: catalog:default' gives 1 error. Quoting the vue catalog value gives 2 findings, which is a false positive and shows the layout dependence that makes it C. The rule passes on the clone.

The overrides leg of tq-15 (C): a pnpm-workspace.yaml override set to 'catalog:' must name a catalog key. It uses the same value-shape source trick. Scratch results: setting chokidar to 'catalog:' in overrides gives 1 error, and deleting the '@types/react-dom' catalog entry gives 1 error from this rule plus 1 from the manifest rule. The rule passes on the clone.

A json_path_absent with "$.dependencies[?match(@, '(file|link):.*')]" over packages/*/package.json, excluding query-codemods and query-test-utils. I confirmed the scope in the clone: 24 packages run publint in test:build, and angular-query-experimental and vue-query-devtools also run it through tsdown publint {strict:true}. Scratch results: 'file:../foo' in react-query dependencies gives 1 error, and 'link:../foo' in angular-query-experimental dependencies gives 1 error. 'link:' in react-query devDependencies gives 0, and 'link:' in the excluded query-codemods dependencies gives 0. The rule passes on the clone.

A json_path_absent with "$.exports..[?match(@, '[^.].*') || match(@, '[.][^/].*')]" over the same 25 publint manifests. Scratch results: query-core default 'build/modern/index.js' gives 1 error, './package.json' -> '../package.json' gives 1 error, and an angular devtools types target without './' gives 1 error. A null export target gives 0. The rule passes on the clone.

A no_bom rule over packages/{preact-query,preact-query-devtools,preact-query-persist-client}/src/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx,mjs,cjs,mts,cts}. I verified in the clone that oxlint.config.ts:453 sets 'unicode-bom': 'error' in preactConfig, that the three preact oxlint configs extend preactConfig, and that their test:oxlint is 'oxlint ./src'. Scratch results: a BOM on preact-query/src/IsRestoringProvider.ts gives 1 error and a BOM on preact-query-devtools/src/PreactQueryDevtools.tsx gives 1 error. A BOM in react-query/src gives 0. The rule passes on the clone.

A for_each_match over packages/svelte-query{,-persist-client}/{src,tests}/**/*.svelte and packages/svelte-query-devtools/src/**/*.svelte. It selects '<script\b' and requires lang="ts", lang='ts' or an unquoted lang=ts. I verified in the clone that all three eslint.config.js files set 'svelte/block-lang': ['error', {script:['ts']}], and I checked the test:eslint dirs and the 50 script tags.
